subject: Finly discovery recap — p95 latency, streaming UX, concurrency
messages:
From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@finly.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 29 Apr 2027 16:02:00 -0700
Subject: Finly discovery recap — p95 latency, streaming UX, concurrency

Hi Alex,

Thanks again for taking the time today — great discussion. Quick recap from our call and proposed next steps below.

Summary of pain points & goals:
- Streaming UX: customers are seeing stutter/lag during live transcript playback; primary goal is smoother token streaming and lower time-to-first-token.
- p95 latency target: Finly is targeting p95 <= 250ms for interactive streaming responses and p95 <= 350ms for longer multi-turn batches.
- Concurrency: expected peak of ~500 concurrent streaming sessions for initial rollout; up to ~2k RPS for non-streaming batch inference during reporting windows.
- Reliability/SLOs: predictable tail-latency and graceful degradation to cheaper model variants when capacity constrained.

Current stack (what you described):
- Prototype on self-hosted open LLMs on EC2 (g5 instances) behind an in-house router; no persistent KV cache and we saw repeated cold starts.
- No autoscaling for streaming workloads today — manual scaling/pager for spikes.

Success criteria for POC:
1) Demonstrate p95 <= 250ms for streaming token delivery under 500 concurrent streams using a realistic prompt distribution.
2) Provide a cost estimate (cost per 1M tokens) in the same ballpark as Finly's target.
3) Integration overhead: SDK + streaming endpoints with minimal code changes and a clear rollback path.

Proposed next steps:
- Run a two-week POC: week 1 = tuning + synthetic load tests; week 2 = small canary with production traffic (5-10%).
- I will send POC plan + load-test template (attached) and a sizing/estimate by EOD tomorrow.
- Please confirm a principal contact for procurement/security questions (SOC 2, data residency, encryption at rest).

Attachments:
- redwood_poc_plan.pdf (POC scope & timeline)
- finly_load_test_template.xlsx (load test scenarios + metrics)

Proposed timeline:
- Confirm POC scope & contacts by Mon 5/3
- Kickoff POC on 5/6
- Load test & tuning complete by 5/13

Let me know if I missed anything or want to adjust the targets. Happy to adjust the plan to match your risk appetite.

Thanks,

Aditya Rao
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
aditya.rao@redwood.com
(415) 555-0199

From: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@finly.com>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Cc: Samantha Lee <samantha.lee@finly.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 29 Apr 2027 18:40:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Finly discovery recap — p95 latency, streaming UX, concurrency

Thanks for the thorough summary, Aditya — this matches our internal notes. A few clarifications and asks:

- Confirming targets: p95 <= 250ms for interactive streaming is right; for longer multi-turn responses we can accept up to 350ms p95 during initial rollout.
- Concurrency: 500 concurrent streaming sessions is our expected peak for MVP; we may see sustained ~1k when we enable certain marketing experiments.
- Cost sensitivity: procurement will want a ballpark for 1M tokens and an estimate for a dedicated capacity option.
- Security: Samantha (cc'd) will own the security questionnaire and needs our SOC 2 and data residency docs.

Quick note: during the call we saw two main failure modes — (1) repeated cold starts when KV cache is cold, (2) spike-induced queuing that created a cascade of retries in our router. Both are major UX hits for streaming.

If you can include a short note in the POC plan about how Redwood addresses cold KV cache and avoids queue amplification under spikes that would be helpful.

Also: we can aim to confirm scope & contacts by EOD Mon 5/3. Assuming that, can we kick off 5/6?

Thanks,
Alex

Alex / Samantha — thanks for the confirmation. A few follow-ups and proposed owners for the POC:

- Security/questions: Samantha — I'll send our SOC 2 report and the data-residency / encryption-at-rest FAQ. Short link: https://redwood.com/soc2-report (attached in metadata).
- Cold KV cache: we'll include a short section in the POC plan describing persistent KV priming and warm-up strategies (prefill windows + prefix caching) and will run tests that show warm vs cold cache p95 impact.
- Queue amplification: POC load tests will include spike scenarios and backpressure settings. We'll instrument router-level queuing metrics and show trade-offs between aggressive batching and tail latency.

Deliverables I will provide by EOD Mon 5/3:
- Final POC plan + staging architecture diagram (redwood_poc_plan.pdf)
- Load test scenarios + template (finly_load_test_template.xlsx)
- Initial sizing & rough cost estimate for dedicated capacity option
- SOC 2 & security doc links (or direct copy for your security team)

Proposed kickoff:
- 5/6: Kickoff + environment access
- 5/7-5/13: Week 1 tuning + synthetic load tests
- 5/14-5/20: Week 2 canary & production validation (adjustable)

I'll also create a HubSpot deal and share the link once the plan is finalized: https://hubspot.redwood/deals/DEAL-2027-FINLY-047

If that timeline looks good I'll lock the kickoff on 5/6 and send calendar invites.

Thanks again — we'll make the tests focused on the p95 streaming targets you need.

Best,
